title: Soft-fallback canary matrix and retro sprint notes (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This is a working canvas for a soft-fallback canary matrix we trialed during the last sprint and the accompanying retrospective notes. The aim is to capture pragmatic decision heuristics (latency/cost/quality), a compact ops checklist for triggering soft fallbacks, cohort-selection heuristics, and a lightweight retro template for future runs.

Scope and motivation
- Focus: staged rollouts for latency-sensitive LLM features where a graceful degradation (soft fallback) keeps user flows functional while minimizing cost and preserving quality.
- Not scope: full A/B statistical analysis cookbook (we link to stats team playbooks). This is a practitioner-facing ops-runbook + sprint retrospective.

Quick TL;DR (actionable heuristics)
- If realtime p95 latency rises >1.5x baseline AND token-unit cost per request jumps >25% → trigger soft fallback slice at 10% and observe for 30m.
- If quality metric (delta in eval pass rate on control prompts) degrades by >3% absolute within 1 hour → rollback model variant from production channel.
- If error rate (5xx/timeout) >0.5% sustained for 10m → pause rollout and open incident channel.

Definitions used in matrix
- Baseline: last stable model variant metrics recorded in Console (model: stable-v1 tag).
- Soft fallback: live routing that sends a fraction of traffic to a cheaper or smaller model variant (e.g., opt-512q -> opt-256q) with output post-processing to match format. Not a full feature rollback.
- Canary stage windows: quick smoke (15–30m), ramp (3–6 hours), steady (24–72 hours).

Soft-fallback canary matrix (operational knobs)
- Initial slice: 1% for smoke (15m), health checks every 1m.
- Slice progression: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% (only if steady for preceding window).
- Observability checks per slice: p50/p95 latency, token cost per request, 5xx rate, quality eval delta, user-facing error signals (helpsdesk tickets, NPS fuzz).
- Soft-fallback parameters: fallback_fraction (percent), fallback_model_variant, kv-cache-compatibility (yes/no), response-postprocess (truncate/normalize), max_tokens_hardcap.

Decision thresholds (examples we used)
- Latency: p95 > 1.5x baseline for 10m → create fallback slice + notify SRE. If p95 > 2x baseline → auto-throttle to previous slice size.
- Cost: per-token cost increase >25% vs baseline for 60m → mark for review; escalate to cost-owner.
- Quality: automated eval suite (N=500 prompts) shows >3% absolute drop in pass rate (or >5% relative drop) within observation window → immediate rollback.
- Error rate: 5xx or timeouts >0.5% sustained for 10m → pause rollout and run incident checklist.

Cohort selection heuristics (how we pick users/slices)
- Prefer deterministic cohorts: user tier, region, device type. Avoid fragile slices (single third-party integration customers) in early smoke.
- For semantic-sensitive changes (e.g., reranker/model upgrade) prioritize high-signal cohorts: top 5k active users, internal dogfooders, and a synthetic test harness that mirrors production queries.
- Always reserve a synthetic-traffic backstop: run a small percentage (1–2%) of artificially generated queries through the new variant in-parallel to surface reproducible failures.

Runbook: what to do during a progressive rollout
1) Pre-launch checklist (day 0):
   - Confirm model version pinned in manifest, fallback variants available and warmed, kv-cache compatibility validated.
   - Start synthetic harness and confirm traffic parity for common endpoints. Tag experiment in Console.
   - Notify stakeholders (oncall, product, SRE, data science) with rollout schedule and expected check-points.
2) Smoke (1% / 15–30m):
   - Monitor p95/p50, errors every 1m; watch cost spikes every 15m.
   - If any threshold breached, incrementally shift fallback_fraction by +9% (soft fall back) and observe for two cycles.
3) Ramp (5–25% / 3–6h):
   - Perform daily quality eval on new requests pulled for labeling.
   - If anomaly signals appear (latency or quality), pause and run focused A/B on flagged cohorts.
4) Steady (50%+ / 24–72h):
   - Enable long-window analytics (24h histograms, user-reported feedback pipeline) and checklist for permanent cutover.

Escalation & communication (ops etiquette)
- First trigger: ping #rollouts + oncall; provide short summary: "canary vX - p95 1.8x baseline, fallback started 10% at 14:12 UTC".
- Second trigger (rollback): open incident in PagerDuty, assign owner, include immediate rollback command and postmortem owner.

Soft-fallback technical notes (ops/dev)
- Routing mechanism: use traffic-router with percent weights; keep model compatibility flags to avoid corrupt KV-cache hits. If KV incompatible, route to cold model with warmup ramp.
- Tokenization/formatting: ensure postprocessing step normalizes tokenization differences (important for rerankers and structured outputs).
- Telemetry tagging: add experiment_id and fallback_fraction to every span/metric to enable quick breakdowns.

Measurement plan for short windows (what to watch first)
- First 30m: p95 latency, error rate, immediate functional checks (synthetic golden queries).
- First 3h: quality regression on golden set, cost delta; human-in-the-loop review of 200 randomly sampled completions.
- 24h: signal stabilization checks: trending p50/p95, user engagement delta, and API quota impacts.

Retrospective skeleton (post-run notes)
- What went well: list specific ops/comms wins (e.g., "fallback slice reduced user errors by X% before rollback").
- What surprised us: unexpected telemetry gaps, missed alerts, misrouted cohorts.
- Concrete improvements: automated gating for metric X, add label Y to spans, create rollback playbook snippet for SRE.
- Action items (owner + due date).

Observations from this sprint (practical run notes)
- The synthetic harness caught a tokenization mismatch in 12m which saved us from a larger rollback. Add it to pre-launch must-haves.
- Our Console dashboard had a blind spot for combined cost*latency signals — create a composite metric (cost-latency index) and surface as an alert.
- Fallback routing entailed a small format mismatch for structured JSON outputs; added a lightweight normalizer in API gateway which fixed downstream parsers.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q: Should soft-fallbacks prefer model quantization variants or smaller architectures? Tradeoffs: quantized models can be faster but sometimes degrade decoding behavior. Need A/B test (owner: Marcos, due: 2026-03-05).
- TODO: Add a synthetic scenario that simulates peak hour token length distributions. (owner: Evan, due: 2026-02-28).
- TODO: Draft a short runbook snippet for support teams describing what to tell customers during a soft-fallback event. (owner: Leila, due: 2026-03-01).

Appendix: quick command references (ops)
- Rollback model: curl -X POST https://console/api/rollouts/rollback -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"stable-v1"}' (ops-only)  <-- placeholder, use CLI tool built into Console
- Start fallback slice: console-cli rollout set-weight --route=/v1/generate --model=new-canary --weight=10

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc intentionally light. Convert to formal runbook after 3 successful runs.
- Add links here to statistical analysis once the stats notebook is ready (ticket RED-7350).

Retrospective snapshot (first-pass)
- Date: 2026-02-10 run
- Outcome: soft fallback reduced error surface and allowed teams to triage without full rollback. Quality dip remained <2% on our golden set (good), but long-tail user reports increased slightly (need better sampling).

End of draft.

(free-form notes and fragments below)
- Heard in retro: "we need a flashcard for stakeholders: what fallback means" -> make a one-pager.
- Consider adding a 'velocity' metric: how fast did p95 move relative to request rate change? Could help distinguish noisy traffic from model regressions.
